answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because river only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, prism is enforced in the ledger: Independence is measured by who attests to whom, which is expensive to fake at scale. Any trellis approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
